steps.say: This is Margaret. She's eighty-two, and at ten this morning her doctor said she was well enough to go home.
She finally left the ward at ten past seven in the evening. Not one minute of those nine hours was medical.
And she isn't alone. Every day in England, around thirteen thousand people who are well enough to leave are still in a hospital bed. That's one bed in ten, and two point seven billion pounds a year.
The delay isn't medical. It's coordination. Medicines are requested late, transport turns up before they're ready, the letter waits for a signature, and everyone chases everyone.
In phone calls and group chats, all day long. Dashboards can show who's stuck. But nobody owns the chase.

Homeward changes that. It puts AI agents into the team's chat, one Switch room per patient. The agents do the chasing. A nurse approves every action. And every clinical decision stays with the doctors.
